title: Data Management

## Overview

The Genetics and Evolution Data Management Plan provides guidance to:

- Manage data storage and archive
- Document our datasets, projects, analyses
- Define our resources

---

## 1. Data Storage Options

Considerations for organizing data storage:

- What are the data that you are storing?
- Hot, Cold, Warm?
- Current, Future access needs?

### 1.1 Shared Drives

- **Use Cases:**
- **Protocol:**
  - Choose the appropriate shared drive: [GE Program Google Shared Drive Inventory](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1et7hupHv0MHEWzbkHK9VAX8ibtgMpLwXuA_UnHZGJ1A/edit?gid=2022882699#gid=2022882699) and follow the naming convention for a given drive
- **Limitations:**
  - Limit on number of files, folders, and shortcuts
  - IF SYNCING WITH COMPUTER:

### 1.2 Google Cloud Buckets

- [CB Genetics Bucket](https://console.cloud.google.com/storage/browser/nwfsc_cb_genetics_shared)
- **Use Cases:**
  - Finished projects that no longer need to be downloaded
  - Archive data that no longer needs to be read or downloaded
  - Data / files that will be worked with in Google Workstation
- **Protocol:**
  - Transfer data with `gcloud storage` command suite (`gcloud storage rsync`)
  - Instructions incoming
  - **Naming convention:** Name your folder `ProjectName_Analysis_Date` or `ProjectName_Archive_Date` depending on whether you have an active project being worked on in Google Workstation (Analysis) or you are storing an archived dataset or analysis (Archive)
- **Limitations:** Costs to read and download the data - new resource / unknown how pay structure will work

### 1.3 Sedna

- **Use Cases:** Active storage for data that is currently being used
- **Protocol:** Put path to your data in inventory spreadsheet (e.g., `Sedna- /home/user/radseq/data`)
- **Limitations:** Space is limited, not a long-term location for archived data

### 1.4 Local Instrument Storage

- **Use Cases:** Storage for data directly from machine (data generation)
- **Protocol:** Indicate folder name and instrument in Local Instrument column
- **Limitations:** Space is limited, not a long-term location for archived data, everyone on the team has access and someone could delete your data

### 1.5 Personal Computer

- **Use Cases:** Active storage for data that is currently being used
- **Protocol:** Put “personal computer” in inventory spreadsheet
- **Limitations:** No one else can access, space is limited, not a long-term location for archived data

### 1.6 NCBI / SRA / Public Repositories

- **Use Cases:** Archive for raw sequencing data and relevant metadata
- **Protocol:** Upload to SRA, delay publishing for 5 years if desired
- All papers using genomic data will have sequences uploaded to SRA - this is our best long-term archive option

| Primary storage location | Secondary storage locations |
|:---:|:---:|
| Shared GDrive (NOT personal MyDrive)<br>Google Bucket<br>SRA (NCBI) | Shared GDrive (NOT personal MyDrive)<br>Google Bucket<br>SRA (NCBI)<br>Sedna<br>QNAP |

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **Shared Drive** | Accessible to team members | Limited File Number<br>Bottleneck transfer size |
| **Google Bucket** | | Not very accessible for analysis (unless using Google Cloud)<br>Cost Associated with Reading and Downloading |
| **QNAP** | Already exists off of sequencer | Does not last forever |
| **Personal Computer** | Free<br>Easy Access for analysis | Not accessible to others |
| **Sedna** | Free | Space can be limited long term |
| **SRA** | Free<br>Accessible<br>Complies with public availability of data | |

## 2. Data Transfer

### 2.1 Rclone

[Rclone](https://rclone.org/) requires configuration the first time you use it. On your local computer, just download rclone and put it in a folder on your computer (documents, desktop, downloads, etc.). See [Instructions to set up Rclone on your local machine or Sedna](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1nn0T0OWEsQCBoCdaH6DSY69lQSbK3XnPlseyyQuU2Lc/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.zbyj83ms3h2).

**Usage:**

```bash
rclone copy /path/to/file.txt google:destination/folder/"quotes for folders with spaces"
